evidence.note: Immediately curled the three pinned libs at exact upstream URLs/versions and ran sha256sum to verify against pinned digests — extracted and empirically confirmed the hardest kill-switch constraint up front.

Built a comprehensive Mastodon-shaped data model and endpoint set (accounts, statuses, timelines, follows, favs, boosts, notifs, polls, lists, admin, OAuth) — a solid working model, but sourced from internal knowledge with no reading of docs.joinmastodon.org anywhere in the run.
Tracked spec seed minimums (≥8 accounts, ≥20 statuses, ≥3 hashtags, ≥2 CW, ≥2 media) and verified counts, showing accurate extraction of explicit numeric constraints.

Verified CSP script-src 'self', session-cookie HttpOnly/SameSite, and checked for forbidden files — partial anti-cheat/realism awareness, but never enumerated the 5 anti-cheat rules or realism gates systematically.

The '19 pytest gates' and the dual auth-plane conflict (UI cookies vs API Bearer) surfaced late via self-reflection/debugging rather than up-front reconnaissance — a gap that forced rework and shows the initial map missed key requirements.

reasoning: The agent cleanly cleared the level-5 anchor: it extracted the explicit hard constraints (vendored-lib paths/hashes/versions, CSP, seed minimums, endpoint list) and formed a working Mastodon API model before major coding, even verifying the hash gate empirically at step 2. It pushes slightly above 5 by empirically confirming several constraints (hashes, seed counts, CSP). But it falls well short of level 8: there is no reading/reconciliation against the real Mastodon wire contract (no spec fetches), no systematic enumeration of the 19 gates or 5 anti-cheat rules, and no probing of offline behavior or the canary-strip detail — with pivotal realities like the dual auth planes discovered through failure rather than research. That places it at a 6.
